question.problem:
Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{90}$ be a random sample of size $n=90$ from a population with a population mean $\mu =92$ and population standard deviation $\sigma =30.$ Find an approximation for the probability that the sample mean is between $90$ and $95.$

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.6\,$ | $\,0.7357\,$ | $\,0.7389\,$ | $\,0.7422\,$ |
| $\,0.7\,$ | $\,0.7673\,$ | $\,0.7704\,$ | $\,0.7734\,$ |
| $\,0.8\,$ | $\,0.7967\,$ | $\,0.7995\,$ | $\,0.8023\,$ |
| $\,0.9\,$ | $\,0.8238\,$ | $\,0.8264\,$ | $\,0.8289\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Suppose that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with a population mean $\mu $ and population standard deviation $\sigma .$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case, we have

$$
n=90,\,\mu =92,\,\sigma =30.
$$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(92,\frac{{30}^{2}}{90}) \\  & ∼N(92,10).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(90<\overset{―}{X}<95).$ So, we convert $\overset{―}{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(90<\overset{―}{X}<95) & =P(\frac{90-92}{\sqrt{10}}<Z<\frac{95-92}{\sqrt{10}}) \\  & =P(-\frac{2}{\sqrt{10}}<Z<\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}) \\  & ≈P(-0.63<Z<0.95) \\  & =P(Z<0.95)-P(Z<-0.63) \\  & =Φ(0.95)-Φ(-0.63)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.95) & =0.8289 \\ Φ(0.63) & =0.7357.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, by the symmetry of the normal distribution, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.63) & =1-Φ(0.63) \\  & =1-0.7357 \\  & =0.2643.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(90<\overset{―}{X}<95) & =Φ(0.95)-Φ(-0.63) \\  & =0.8289-0.2643 \\  & =0.5646.\end{aligned}
$$
